articles.title: France falls into recession after far-left riots break out across country in blow to Emmanuel Macron
articles.description: France has fallen into recession after the European nation's economy shrank by more than the predicted figures. Emmanuel Macron is said to be facing a crisis after the economy plunged by 0.2 per cent in the third quarter between July and September. The shrinking of France's economy is bigger than the predicted 0.1 per cent figure. New revised estimates also show figures fell in the second quarter as well as the third by 0.02 per cent. France was originally predicted to see a flatline for the same period. Following the revision of the stats, Europe’s third-largest economy now meets the definition of a technical recession. Marie Leclair of France’s statistics agency INSEE confirmed: "We now have a very slight decline in GDP in the second quarter." Senior economist at Dutch bank ING Charlotte de Montpellier said of the figures: "It has technically been in recession since the beginning of the year." She added: "The outlook for 2027 remains very gloomy. Salaried employment fell by 94,400 jobs over the past year. "The situation is even worse in the private sector, where 109,000 jobs were lost over the same period. "The weakening labour market will increasingly weigh on household confidence, income and consumption. "Financing conditions also remain difficult, while uncertainty over future taxes and public spending is exceptionally high." The country's deficit is also poised to hit 5.5 per cent of GDP this year, the highest in the euro area. The shrinking economic growth comes as Mr Macron faces growing mass protests over high fuel prices. One protester was killed, and more than 100 others were injured during the nationwide demonstrations that commenced in September. Police deployed tear gas in an attempt to disperse the protesters, the "yellow vests". Demonstrations took place in Porte Maillot, Bastille Square and Champs-Elysees in Paris. According to the interior ministry, around 244,000 people took part in around 2,000 protests across the country. A crowd of at least 1,000 protesters also gathered in front of Elysee Palace, calling for Mr Macron to resign. Ms Montpellier predicted the French will be "heading to the polls" against the backdrop of a "weakening economy" for Mr Macron. She concluded: "It is difficult to identify a driver capable of generating a meaningful recovery in domestic demand over the next few quarters. "France will enter next year without economic momentum. Even if quarterly growth turns slightly positive again, this will not be enough to produce solid annual growth. "We expect GDP to grow by just 0.4 per cent on average in 2027, with risks still tilted to the downside." Our Standards: The GB News Editorial Charter
